title: Nullable types and safe calls
context: How do nullable types, safe calls, the Elvis operator and the not-null assertion work in Kotlin, and when should you avoid `!!`?

refs.title: Atomic Kotlin (book) by Bruce Eckel & Svetlana Isakova

answer: A type ending in `?` can hold null. The compiler stops you from calling members on it directly. `?.` calls a member only when the value is not null, and otherwise the whole chain returns null. `?:` gives a fallback when the left side is null. `!!` asserts non-null and throws NullPointerException if it is wrong. Avoid `!!` in production code: prefer a smart cast after a check, `?.let`, or an Elvis with a meaningful default or an error.

points.title: Null-safety in the type
points.why: Nullability is part of the type, so the compiler forces a check before member access.

points.title: Avoid !!
points.why: `!!` moves the null check to run time and throws NullPointerException.

points.title: Elvis for defaults
points.why: `?:` gives a fallback or an early exit when the value is missing.
